_comment: BAND-SPLIT. Band-local clusters for band4_upper_meadows_ironwood. `order` is this entry's index in the merged array and is the ONLY thing that decides merge position -- never file order, never band order. Existing entries keep the index they had before the split because the merged array order is the order props are added to the scene tree, and Godot silently auto-renames same-named siblings by that order. A new entry in this band takes an unused order in this band's reserved range 4000-4999, which no other band can collide with; do not renumber an existing one.

clusters.name: ridge_patrol_camp
clusters._why: GATE-D4/prompt 65: spec Band 4 names 'ruined watch/occupation traces' and 'Team Tether patrol camps' among the region's regional identity and this band had zero prop clusters authored at package start. Sited on the watchtower spur beside the new patrol trainer (trainers.json order 4000) and 46m from captain_ridge -- the garrison the trainer belongs to, read the same way `old_quarry.gd`'s `quarry_station` and `ranger_camp` clusters read their own sites: a posting left mid-shift, not a stage set. Same prop family both of those already use (D24, one prop family) -- nothing here is new. A crate and barrel for supply, a bag and rope for gear, a whetstone for the same reason the quarry crew left one, and the axe standing in for a Team Tether tool rather than a mining one: the composition differs by what a patrol carries, not by a new mesh.
clusters._why_r7: VP4-CORRIDOR round 7 (JUDGE-round6.md / time-boxed dispatch). Three real-rendered camera candidates from the walked pt11->pt15 segment (eye=pt13/pt12/pt11, look held at pt15 or at the fire's own exact coordinate) all failed to show the camp: unproject_position() and a direct crop of the saved PNG both agreed the fire/tent never appear, even when the camera looks directly at the fire's own coordinate at 45m from the closest trail point (pt14) -- a result that was not fully diagnosed within this round's time-box (a `get_viewport()` identity check was queued but not completed). Rather than keep spending the round's remaining budget on that mystery, applied the coordinator's own explicit fallback: 'move the camp's dressing anchor... 5-10m toward the route... a legitimate corridor fix'. Every prop below (rest/craft_at/creature_bed included) shifted by the same rigid (dx=-6.83, dz=-1.52) -- 7m toward pt14 along the pt14->old-centroid bearing -- preserving the whole camp's internal layout exactly. `clearings[4000]` and the round-4/7 rock-shelf anchor in this band's vegetation.json move with it.
clusters._why_vp5: VP5 visual-parity pass. This is the Upper Meadows' only authored camp, and it was built as five props strung along the ruin wall in a straight line with the fire off to one side -- legible as a supply drop, not as a camp. The supply pile now sits together W-SW of the fire, seating is arranged tangentially on both sides of it (the stool moved, a log seat added), firewood was added radial to the fire, and the whetstone -- the patrol's own grindstone -- sits south where the pile used to trail off in a line. The cluster also gains this band's only `rest` block: a named `rest` site the player could not previously use.

rest._why: VP5. `ridge_patrol_camp` is the only authored camp in Upper Meadows and, until now, could not be rested at -- every other camp cluster in the chapter (band1's trail_camp, band3's riverwatch_rest and the_waystop, band4's own highfield_stockcamp) carries a `rest` block and this one did not. Sited 2.0m SE of the fire, in the open SE quarter clear of the supply pile (W-SW), the tent (west, against the ruin) and both seats, the same clearance geometry `camp.gd` and `rest_point.gd` use at every other camp. `bed_index: -16` is the next free reserved index -- the chapter's other four beds already hold -11 through -15 -- and `scripts/world/rest_point.gd` builds this exactly like those four: same mechanic, same `night_rest.gd` call, no second rest system.
rest.label: Rest until morning

creature_bed._why: The bed sits in the open SE quarter of the camp, clear of the fire, both seats, the supply pile and the tent -- its own quarter the way `highfield_stockcamp`'s bed keeps its own quarter on the far side of that camp's fire from its tent. `bed_index -16` is the next free reserved index after this chapter's existing -11..-15.

props._why: VP5. Regrouped W-SW of the fire, 3.0m off it, as the anchor of one touching supply pile with the barrel, bag and rope -- the post's own supply crate, still set against the ruin's own side of the camp
VP5. Set touching the crate, one load rather than a scatter
VP5. Leaning against the crate -- a picket's kit, dropped rather than packed, the same detail that reads 'abandoned' at the quarry and the ranger camp, told a third time
VP5. Coiled at the pile's own edge -- what tied a watch-line to the ruin above before the ruin stopped being watched
VP5. The patrol's own grindstone, 4m south of the fire and off the supply pile -- set down and not picked back up, same reasoning as the quarry crew's own whetstone

leaning against the crate, pitched off vertical -- the one tool that names a patrol rather than a dig, the same lean `quarry_station`'s pickaxe uses for the same reason. VP5: kept at the same offset from the crate it leaned on before, moving with the pile

SITE-DRESSING: the D1 trail-camp's own solved fire (Bonfire_Fire.obj's real `Fire` surface + ignite() + campfire_glow.gd's light/embers/smoke), scaled down further than band1's -- a patrol posting keeps a smaller fire than a rest camp.
props._why_reclustered: AUDIT-E E4 (ralph/reports/audit/E-2026-08-31.md): sited 3.5-5.4m from the crate/barrel/rope/whetstone supply pile against the ruin, this read as two unrelated groups -- 'props ... sit in a straight line ... instead of clustered around the firepit'. Moved 1.0m (dx-0.8, dz-0.6) toward the pile, staying on its own open ground short of the ruin wall the pile is set against (unchanged: crate/barrel/rope/whetstone/axe keep every stated relationship to each other and to the ruin) -- now 2.6-3.6m from crate/barrel/whetstone and 1.0-1.6m from the nearer axe/bag, close enough that the fire reads as what the pile is arranged around rather than a second, separate lit prop nearby. `campfire_stone_ring` and `Stool` below move the same 1.0m so the fire, its ring and its one seat keep the geometry `_why` already describes.
props._why_glow_scale: AUDIT-E E4: the fire is present and correctly targeted by 08-ridge-camp-fire's own capture stand but 'mostly hidden behind the player character's own head', too small/dim to register at normal viewing size. The log pile keeps its own smaller `scale` (a patrol keeps a smaller fire than a rest camp, per the note above) -- `glow_scale` only grows the light/embers `campfire_glow.gd` builds around it (props.gd's own overlay counter-scale means the glow was rendering at every other camp's absolute size regardless, so growing the mesh alone would not have fixed legibility). 1.8x brings the light range to 14.4m and the light energy/ember count up with it, at night (this stand's own capture pass), without changing the fire prop's own footprint or touching any other camp's fire (every other `glow: "campfire"` caller in the chapter keeps the 1.0 default).

props._why: SITE-DRESSING: the D1 fire-ring mesh (owner-referenced, already committed under assets/props/generated_camp -- no new generation), scaled to this smaller fire's own footprint the same way band1 matched it to its six-stone predecessor. AUDIT-E E4: moved with `Bonfire_Fire` above, same offset, so the ring keeps matching the brazier's own footprint.
props._why_vp5: VP5. Grown from 0.55 to 0.85 to match the brazier's own enlargement; sink_m raised to 0.03 to keep the ring's base seated against the taller fire.

props._why: one seat, facing the fire across it -- the piece that turns a fire into a place someone sits rather than a lit prop. Same model band1's trail_camp already uses for its own second seat.
props._why_vp5: VP5. Moved to sit tangential to the fire 2.6m NE, opposite the new log seat, instead of the straight line the props formerly ran in along the ruin.

props._why: SITE-DRESSING: the D1 owner-referenced tent mesh (already committed, no new generation), scaled down from band1's 1.05 -- a patrol keeps one small shelter, not a rest camp's. Placed against the ruin behind the crate/barrel, mouth turned toward the fire so the tent and the fire read as one posting instead of two unrelated objects. `sink_m` copied from band1's own measured fix for this same mesh's raised local origin.

VP5. A second seat, tangential to the fire 2.7m NW, opposite the stool -- one stool alone read as a single perch rather than a manned camp with somewhere to sit. Kenney's textured CC0 log, the same mesh every other camp in the chapter uses for this role.
VP5. Firewood south of the fire, radial rather than tangential -- band1's own rule, for the opposite reason its seats obey.

VP5 round8. A patroller's own kit set down beside the bed rather than at the supply pile 5m west -- this is the only camp in the chapter with the player's own creature bed, and the bar for this site is 'the bed and fire are the subject, supplies secondary'. One bag at the sleeping spot, unpaired from the crate/barrel/rope group, keeps the west-side supplies reading as secondary rather than the pile the camp is arranged around.

SITE-DRESSING: first of three stepping stones on the south-west approach (the capture viewpoint's own eye line, tools/_capture_band4_sites.gd `ridge-patrol-camp`) -- ground props.gd/vegetation.json cannot touch a worn-path texture, so the beaten route reads as a line of trodden stone instead. Same Rock_Medium family band1's own fire-ring arc uses; a rotation/scale distinct from its two siblings below so the line does not repeat one stone three times.
SITE-DRESSING: second stepping stone, midway between the approach and the fire.
SITE-DRESSING: third stepping stone, closing the line onto the camp's own supply pile -- the arriving path connection the ridge camp had none of.

clusters.name: highfield_stockcamp
clusters._why:
T5-CADENCE. The first of four beats closing T4-REGIONS' worst measurement in the chapter -- 1161m of structurally empty spine (232s walking, 166s at sprint cruise) through the middle of the longest band, robust at 3x notice radii, immediately before the endgame. The audit's own verdict: 'A player who is going to put the Meadows down will put it down here.'

It also closes the band's OTHER standing FAIL. Until this cluster, band 4 had exactly ONE prop cluster in 3436m -- `ridge_patrol_camp`, which is Team Tether's own posting at the far end -- so the Upper Meadows offered nowhere to stop, and exit criterion E's 'a sensible camp/recovery opportunity' had no candidate at all. This is a camp, and (see its `rest` block) it works.

WHOSE CAMP. `pasture_drover_juno` already stands on this road at arc 899 and `captain_field` takes his title from the high pasture (data/items/items.json's `field_sigil`: 'the ploughed-furrow device of the high pasture posting'). This is the other end of Juno's road: the summer stock camp the drovers keep while the herd is up. Still in use, unlike the ranger camp and the quarry -- which is the point, because the chapter's back half needs one place that is not abandoned.

SITED at (275.0,5653.7): the flattest 7m pad within 26m of the spine here, measured at 0.70m of relief and 9.0 degrees worst slope by tools/_probe_cadence_flat.gd. Band 1's trail camp took three relocations to learn that a camp on a 1.2m drop reads as a slope with objects on it; this one was swept first.

rest._why: The Upper Meadows' rest point. See `scripts/world/rest_point.gd` for what the offer is and why every authored camp now makes it. Sited 1.9m south-east of the fire, clear of the ring (scale 1.0, ~2.0m across) and on the opposite side from the bench, exactly the geometry `camp.gd` uses for its own.
rest.label: Rest until morning

creature_bed._why: A working creature bed on the far side of the fire from the tent. This is the only one between the band 3 crossing and the stronghold, which makes it the place a player prepares for two captains and three Sigils -- exit criterion H3's expedition decision, in the band VISION §3 says should be pressing hardest on the five. 4.6m from the fire, 2.2m from the stool, and its own quarter of the camp so the sleeping body is never inside another prop.

props._why: the camp's centre. The owner-referenced ring already committed under assets/props/generated_camp (docs/ASSET_LEDGER.md) and already used by band 1's trail camp and band 4's own ridge posting -- third use, nothing generated. Scale 1.0 (~2.0m) sits between band 1's rest camp (1.05) and the patrol posting's (0.55): a working camp, not a picket's brazier.

the fire inside it -- Bonfire_Fire.obj's real `Fire` surface lit through `glow: campfire`, plus campfire_glow.gd's light, embers and smoke. The smoke column is what makes this camp findable from the trail 7m below it, which is the whole reason a camp closes a dead stretch rather than merely sitting in one.

the drovers' shelter, mouth turned toward the fire. Same owner-referenced tent mesh band 1 and band 4's ridge camp already place, at band 1's own scale rather than the patrol's smaller 0.85 -- people live up here for a season. `sink_m` is band 1's measured compensation for this mesh's raised local origin.
a long seat facing the fire across it, tangential so its 2.78m length runs perpendicular to the radius -- band 1's trail-camp rule, for the same reason
a second, smaller seat on the fire's other side; two ways to sit is what `ranger_camp`'s round 3 identified as the difference between a camp and a supply drop
water, kept at the tent's end rather than the fire's
stores, touching the barrel so the pair reads as one load
somebody's kit against the crate -- and set down rather than dropped, because this camp is tended
a drover's own tool, and the piece that makes the Craft offer at this fire read as something the site supports
upright and within reach of the bench

firewood, radial to the fire rather than tangential -- the opposite rule from the seats, for the opposite reason (band 1's own note). Kenney's textured log, the CC0 mesh band 1's camp uses after the untextured nature-pack one was replaced.
the clearing's own edge, past the bed so the camp has a back to it
tall tuft on the trail side -- the foreground the camp is seen past on the approach

clusters.name: severed_conduit_post
clusters._why:
T5-CADENCE, third beat of the band-4 dead run (the second is the herd bull, spawns.json order 4101). Exit criterion E3: 'Team Tether presence visibly changes the land -- pylons, hardware, drained ground escalating toward the stronghold', and fun-rebuild §12's vocabulary names 'Team Tether pylon' and 'Team Tether camp' outright. Band 4 had neither anywhere in the 1161m: the player crosses the whole eastern sweep of the band before the endgame without meeting one thing that says the faction is ahead of them.

This is a cable post on the high ground -- crates, two coils of conduit line, an anchor stone and a staked banner -- on the run that carried the Meadows' drained energy toward the Hall, cut and abandoned. It deliberately does NOT stand a pylon: `severed_spokes.gd::_build_pylons` is the shared builder for those (borrowed already by old_quarry.gd and stronghold.gd) and hanging a 12m pylon run here is a code change in a file this lane could not verify visually. Recorded as the better version of this beat in ralph/reports/handover-T5-CADENCE-2026-08-30.md rather than half-built.

Sited at (372,6068), 0.78m of relief over a 6m pad (tools/_probe_cadence_sites.gd) -- the flattest ground measured in the eastern sweep, which is where a cable anchor would actually be set.

props._why: the post's own crate, upright and squared to the run
emptied and left -- the line's spares went where the line's crew went
water for a crew on ground with none, touching the crate
a coil of the conduit line itself, off the drum and never run

props.name: conduit_coil_2
props._why: a second coil beside the first. Its own `name` because props.gd would otherwise let Godot rename the duplicate to an unreadable id, which is invisible in the world and useless in a probe.
Team Tether's mark, staked at the post and leaning. Same castle Banner module and same oxblood hex (#7a2430) as this chapter's other three faction sites -- one mesh, one colour, no new asset.
the anchor stone the line was set against, at the meadow scatter's own 0.3 so it reads as the ground's rather than as brought here
a second stone on the far side, different mesh and rotation
leaning against the crate, for setting anchors into hard ground -- the tool that names the work, the same lean `quarry_station` and the haulage wreck both use

clusters.name: the_wind_overlook
clusters._why:
T5-CADENCE, fourth beat of the band-4 dead run. Fun-rebuild §12's 'overlook' and 'landmark with visible reward'; exit criterion E1, which asks that a player can answer 'where did I come from / where can I go' without the minimap. T4-REGIONS scored band 4's route hierarchy PARTIAL for exactly that reason -- its three named regions 'cluster at the band's two ends ... The 1161m between has no landmark, and the watchtower -- the one thing built to be seen from far off -- sits past the dead stretch, not inside it.'

This is the crest where the road turns off the Highfield and the Ridgeline Watch first comes into view ahead: bedrock the trail bends around, two taller marker stones a drover set to keep the road findable in hill fog, and somebody's pack. Old, ordinary, and nobody's faction -- deliberately NOT invented lore. The Meadows has drovers and a drove road; waymarkers are what drove roads have.

THE MARKER STONES USE `scale_xyz`, which is the one thing here worth flagging. Rock_Medium_* are boulders, raw 3.2 x 2.3 x 3.0m (measured), and uniform scale can only ever produce a bigger or smaller boulder. props.gd's `scale_xyz` exists for precisely this ('a shape correction no single uniform number can express' -- its own header), so the two markers are narrowed and raised into standing-stone proportions instead of a new mesh being sourced. It does stretch their normal maps, and that is a real cost: VISUAL NOTE for the judge lane, flagged rather than hidden.

IT PAYS (exit criterion G9): harvest.json order 4031, a Greater Orb, the one band 4 had none of.

props._why: the crest's own bedrock, the largest thing here and what the trail bends around. Scale 0.95 (~3.1 x 2.1 x 2.8m) -- far past the meadow scatter's 0.14-0.19, which is the point: this is geology, not a stone in the grass.
second of the outcrop, downwind side
third, on the uphill approach, so the group has a near side and a far side rather than reading as a pile

props.name: waymarker_north
props._why: the first of the two set markers: same boulder mesh, narrowed and raised through `scale_xyz` into a 1.5 x 2.5 x 1.4m standing stone. Taller than the trainer, which is what makes it read as placed rather than fallen, and what carries it from the trail below. Its own `name` for the duplicate-model reason props.gd documents.

props.name: waymarker_south
props._why: the second marker, the pair that makes a line and therefore a direction. Shorter than its sibling and turned across it, because two identical stones read as a gate and a gate is a different thing from a waymark.
set down between the markers and the bedrock -- a traveller stopped here, which is the difference between a rock formation and a place
tall tuft on the open side, so the stones stand in something
the crest's scrubby uphill edge

clusters.name: ridge_road_picket
clusters._why:
T5-CADENCE, fifth and last beat of the band-4 dead run, and the one that hands the player over to the Ridge Captain. Exit criterion F2 asks that Team Tether escalate 'rumor -> evidence -> confrontation -> operation -> hierarchy -> Warden, never as unrelated fights': the severed conduit post 500m back is the operation, and this is the hierarchy closing in -- a roadblock across the trainer road, 300m below `captain_ridge` and the ridge patrol camp.

Crates and a felled log dragged across the road, a brazier still ringed, a stool, and the banner staked square to the road bearing. Same castle Banner module, same oxblood, same fire-and-ring pair every other posting in the chapter uses; nothing here is a new mesh.

UNMANNED, and that is a file-ownership fact, not a design one. A picket standing on this barricade is the obviously better version and it is one row in data/config/bands/band4_upper_meadows_ironwood/trainers.json -- a file two other lanes hold this session (ralph/T3-ACTIVITIES and ralph/T1-CREATURE-RIG). This lane stayed off it and recorded the row it would have written in ralph/reports/handover-T5-CADENCE-2026-08-30.md. T4-REGIONS' eighth finding -- band 4 runs one trainer per 859m, the sparsest in the chapter -- is still open, and this site is where the cheapest fix for it goes.

Sited at (-6.7,6299.7), the flattest 5m pad within 22m of the spine here (0.88m relief, tools/_probe_cadence_flat.gd) -- a barricade wants level ground, or it reads as debris that slid there.

props._why: the barricade's own crate, squared to the road bearing rather than to the world -- a thing stacked on purpose

props.name: barricade_crate_2
props._why: the second crate of the pair, same bearing, touching the first so the two read as one wall. Its own `name` for the duplicate-model reason props.gd documents.
a felled log dragged across the road behind the crates -- the piece that makes this a block rather than a supply stack. Kenney's textured CC0 log, as at band 1's camp and the north-bank cutting.
water for a posting that has to stand here all day

staked at the barricade's open end and squared to the same road bearing (128) as the log. Whose road this is, said the way the chapter says it everywhere else: the castle kit's Banner retinted oxblood (#7a2430).
the picket's brazier ring, scaled to a held checkpoint's small fire the way `relay_approach_checkpoint`'s is (0.5) rather than a rest camp's
the fire in it -- the same solved combination every other posting uses, and at night the thing that tells the player from 200m down the road that the way ahead is held
one seat by the brazier, on the barricade's own side of it
a picket's kit, against the barrel
what dragged the log across, still tied to nothing
